security_audit.summary: All 41 static alerts are false positives caused by Markdown code formatting, relative documentation links, homepage metadata, and a documented local save path. The skill provides planning guidance only and explicitly directs the agent to treat imported exports as untrusted input. No prompt injection, credential access, data exfiltration, command execution, or path-traversal behavior was found.

remediation.issue: Static scanners misclassify Markdown code delimiters and relative links as executable commands or traversal.
remediation.suggestion: Use scanner-aware documentation formatting or tune the scanner to distinguish Markdown links, code literals, and static workspace paths from executable operations.

remediation.issue: The skill may process email engagement exports supplied by users.
remediation.suggestion: Keep the existing untrusted-input instruction and require explicit user confirmation before saving results or using optional platform integrations.

content.user_title: Build a consent-aware email reactivation plan
content.value_statement: Inactive subscribers can reduce deliverability and make list decisions difficult. This skill creates a staged, consent-aware plan to recover interested subscribers and suppress the rest.
actual_capabilities: Defines a lapsed cohort using a stated no-open or no-click window.
Creates a staged win-back offer ladder with timing, triggers, and exit conditions.
Defines a re-permission action that creates a fresh opt-in signal.
Sets a final rule that returns re-permissioned subscribers or suppresses non-responders.
Labels cohort conclusions as measured, user-provided, or estimated.
Produces handoff facts for consent, lifecycle, and preference-management workflows.
limitations: It designs a program but does not send email or change an email platform.
It cannot verify lawful basis, consent records, or platform data without user-provided information.
It does not calculate email quality scores or enforce final compliance gates.
It does not replace legal review for consent, privacy, or marketing regulations.

use_cases.title: Recover inactive subscribers
use_cases.description: Build a measured win-back sequence for subscribers who stopped opening or clicking email.

use_cases.title: Clean a declining email list
use_cases.description: Set a final suppression process that avoids bulk deletion and preserves clear terminal states.

use_cases.title: Prepare a re-permission program
use_cases.description: Define the confirmation action and operational handoffs needed before returning subscribers to regular nurture.

prompt_templates.title: Start with a cohort
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a reactivation plan for subscribers with no opens in 90 days. We use an email platform and have no discount available.

prompt_templates.title: Add an offer ladder
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a three-step win-back offer ladder for subscribers with no clicks in 180 days. Include timing, triggers, and stop rules.

prompt_templates.title: Plan re-permission
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a re-permission campaign for our inactive newsletter cohort. Define the confirmation action, consent handoff, and suppression rule.

prompt_templates.title: Handle incomplete data
prompt_templates.prompt: Our engagement export is missing, but our policy says to suppress non-responders after 30 days. Create an estimated reactivation plan and list open questions.

output_examples.input: Create a plan for subscribers with no opens in 90 days.
output: Cohort: subscribers with no opens for 90 days, excluding suppressed and hard-bounced contacts.
Ladder: reminder, optional incentive, then a final confirmation message.
Terminal rule: return confirmed subscribers to nurture and suppress non-responders after the defined window.

output_examples.input: We need a re-permission sweep without a discount.
output: Use a value-focused re-engagement message followed by a clear confirmation request.
Record the confirmation action through the consent workflow.
Cap contacts at three messages and honor existing send limits.

best_practices: Use a documented cohort window and exclude already suppressed or hard-bounced contacts.
Require an affirmative re-permission action before returning a subscriber to regular nurture.
Set one terminal state for every subscriber and record unresolved data as an open question.
anti_patterns: Do not keep sending to inactive subscribers without an escalation limit or stop rule.
Do not treat an email open alone as fresh consent.
Do not design suppression rules when lawful basis or consent records are unknown.

faq.question: Does this skill send the campaign?
faq.answer: No. It creates a plan and does not send email or modify an email platform.

faq.question: What data should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide the inactivity window, available incentive, suppression policy, and engagement export when available.

faq.question: Can it work without an engagement export?
faq.answer: Yes. It can create an estimated plan from your stated cohort definition and identify missing data.

faq.question: Does it manage consent records?
faq.answer: No. It defines the re-permission action and expects a consent workflow to record the outcome.

faq.question: How many messages should a reactivation ladder include?
faq.answer: The skill generally recommends three to four touches, with a clear stop rule.

faq.question: Does it provide legal compliance advice?
faq.answer: No. Use legal review for applicable consent, privacy, and marketing requirements.
